theme: Ugin: The Spirit Dragon — From the Ur-Dragon's Brood to the End of the Meditation Realm
status: PROPOSED LORE DECK #9 — awaiting Cory's approval
narrator_note: The Ur-Dragon is the primordial progenitor of Ugin and Nicol Bolas, WUBRG commander for biography framing. No official source identifies it as explicitly female; call it a progenitor rather than literal mom.

beats.title: I. Egg-stones and brothers: birth on Dominaria, their first wound, and the Elder Dragon War

cards.name: The Elder Dragon War
cards.why: Retrospective Saga anchoring the ancient catastrophe that changed dragonkind; the war was instigated by Nicol Bolas, not by Ugin.

cards.name: Arcades Sabboth
cards.why: Ugin and Nicol's elder brother, who sheltered the young twins and taught them how mortals and dragons coexist.

cards.name: Chromium
cards.why: Another surviving Elder Dragon and sibling; a witness to how the twins differed from the older generation.

cards.name: Palladia-Mors
cards.why: Their terrifying elder sister, whose disdain for the smaller twins helped shape Nicol's insecurity.

cards.name: Vaevictis Asmadi
cards.why: A member of the same primordial Elder Dragon lineage; contextual extended family, not evidence that he accompanied Ugin.

cards.name: Piru, the Volatile
cards.why: Elder Dragon spawned by the Ur-Dragon, Chromium's mate and survivor of the Elder Dragon War; contextual family history.

cards.name: Nicol Bolas
cards.why: The original Legends depiction of Ugin's twin, born from the same egg; his fear and ambition begin the central rivalry.

cards.name: Nicol Bolas, the Ravager
cards.why: A later portrait of the twin's controlling, predatory nature; visual retrospective, not a distinct early-life incident.

beats.title: II. A different road: Ugin's spark, discovery, ghostfire and philosophy

cards.name: Ghostfire
cards.why: Ugin's signature invisible flame, whose colorless expression illustrates his transcendence of individual colors.

cards.name: Spatial Contortion
cards.why: Its original flavor is attributed to Ugin about the dangers of the Blind Eternities, contextualizing planeswalker travel.

cards.name: Scroll of Fate
cards.why: An Ugin-attributed philosophical quote in its Commander 2019 printing; symbolic meditation, not a literal artifact he owned.

beats.title: III. Tarkir: Ugin's draconic essence and the dragon tempests

cards.name: Dragon Tempest
cards.why: The storms born from Ugin's magic that populate Tarkir with dragons.

cards.name: Dragonstorm
cards.why: An older spell chosen as a visual shorthand for Tarkir's dragon-generating magical phenomenon; not a specific dated incident.

cards.name: Fearsome Awakening
cards.why: Its Fate Reforged flavor directly connects the dragonstorms to Ugin's presence.

cards.name: Soul Summons
cards.why: A Fate Reforged card that explicitly says Ugin's magic also reached Tarkir's humanoid clans.

cards.name: Ugin's Mastery
cards.why: Articulates the Spirit Dragon's colorless and manifest philosophy; a later card, used as a thematic portrait.

beats.title: IV. The Eldrazi dilemma: Ugin, Sorin, Nahiri, and the prison on Zendikar

cards.name: Sorin Markov
cards.why: The vampire planeswalker who joined Ugin and Nahiri in the ancient plan to contain the three titans.

cards.name: Nahiri, the Lithomancer
cards.why: The planeswalker who built the hedron network on her home plane at Ugin's direction.

cards.name: Emrakul, the Aeons Torn
cards.why: One of the three actual Eldrazi titans trapped by the trio. Intentionally retains a banned card for complete lore.

cards.name: Kozilek, Butcher of Truth
cards.why: The second titan imprisoned within Zendikar's hedron network.

cards.name: Ulamog, the Infinite Gyre
cards.why: The third titan imprisoned within Zendikar's hedron network.

cards.name: Aligned Hedron Network
cards.why: A direct card representation of the hedron prison Ugin and his allies designed.

cards.name: Perilous Vault
cards.why: Its original flavor explicitly credits Ugin with aligning hedrons to channel Zendikar's energy.

cards.name: Hedron Archive
cards.why: Original flavor quotes Ugin explaining to Jace that the Eldrazi could be held captive.

cards.name: Ugin's Construct
cards.why: Its Fate Reforged flavor directly explains that Ugin learned lithomancy while setting the Eldrazi trap.

cards.name: Dreamstone Hedron
cards.why: An actual hedron artifact illustrating the Eldrazi's strange ability to exploit prison magic; technology context.

cards.name: Lithomancer's Focus
cards.why: Original Battle for Zendikar card with Ugin's direct comment on the effectiveness of Nahiri's hedrons.

beats.title: V. Brothers at war: the original tragedy, Sarkhan's rewrite, and the dragonlord future

cards.name: Crux of Fate
cards.why: The defining clash above Tarkir: Bolas strikes Ugin down in the original history; Sarkhan's later intervention changes that outcome.

cards.name: Bitter Revelation
cards.why: Its Khans printing speaks to Ugin's apparent corpse and belongs to the erased original Tarkir timeline.

cards.name: Yasova Dragonclaw
cards.why: The ancient Temur khan who witnessed the confrontation and received Nicol Bolas's manipulative visions.

cards.name: Sarkhan Vol
cards.why: The time-traveling planeswalker whose connection to Ugin's whispered summons is pivotal.

cards.name: Sarkhan Unbroken
cards.why: Sarkhan after rewriting Tarkir's fate; a character portrait of his changed history.

cards.name: Ugin's Nexus
cards.why: The original Khans card marking the temporal nexus where Ugin's voice ceased for Sarkhan.

cards.name: Nexus of Fate

cards.name: Fate Forgotten
cards.why: The Dragons of Tarkir printing explicitly acknowledges that saving Ugin rewrote Tarkir's history.

cards.name: Scion of Ugin
cards.why: Its original flavor describes Ugin's centuries-long slumber in the protective cocoon Sarkhan made.

cards.name: Tormenting Voice
cards.why: The Dragons of Tarkir printing speaks of the centuries Ugin spent unconscious while Bolas operated freely.

cards.name: Sarkhan's Triumph

cards.name: Ugin, the Spirit Dragon
cards.why: Ugin surviving and returning; direct planeswalker portrait placed at the altered-history awakening.

cards.name: Dragonlord Atarka
cards.why: One of the five dragonlord lineages empowered by continued storms after Sarkhan saved Ugin.

cards.name: Dragonlord Dromoka
cards.why: The protective brood whose ascent follows the surviving dragonstorms.

cards.name: Dragonlord Kolaghan
cards.why: The swift brood arising from Ugin's restored dragonstorm ecology.

cards.name: Dragonlord Ojutai
cards.why: The scholarly brood whose rule is part of Tarkir's rewritten world.

cards.name: Dragonlord Silumgar
cards.why: The ruthless Sultai-replacing brood of the restored dragonstorm world.

beats.title: VI. Ugin's long plan: the Eldrazi release, Azor's ancient trap, and Bolas's defeat

cards.name: Ugin's Insight
cards.why: Ugin's original dialogue warns Jace not to focus on Ulamog and forget the other two titans.

cards.name: Dispel
cards.why: The Battle for Zendikar printing quotes Jace rejecting Ugin's suggestion to return the Eldrazi to stasis.

cards.name: Fall of the Titans
cards.why: The Gatewatch destroys Ulamog and Kozilek, taking a different path from Ugin's preferred stasis plan.

cards.name: Kozilek's Return
cards.why: The titan's reappearance during the Zendikar crisis that Ugin had tried to contain.

cards.name: Azor, the Lawbringer
cards.why: Ugin's ancient collaborator on the Immortal Sun gambit against Nicol Bolas, revealed in later story.

cards.name: The Immortal Sun
cards.why: Azor's device fueled by his relinquished spark, originally part of an unrealized Bolas trap coordinated with Ugin.

cards.name: Finale of Revelation
cards.why: The War of the Spark flavor explicitly says Ugin understood Bolas's Meditation Realm gem could undo him.

cards.name: Prison Realm
cards.why: The printed War of the Spark story card for the final confinement of the desparked Nicol Bolas under Ugin's watch.

cards.name: Nicol Bolas, Dragon-God
cards.why: Bolas's attempted restoration to godhood, the crisis Ugin's long preparation addresses.

cards.name: The Elderspell
cards.why: The dangerous spell at the center of Bolas's attempt to harvest planeswalker sparks.

cards.name: Ugin, the Ineffable
cards.why: Ugin's War of the Spark planeswalker portrait, printed in the showdown's set.

cards.name: Sarkhan's Catharsis
cards.why: The card's original flavor has Sarkhan confront Bolas over past damage; Ugin's rescue made this opposition possible.

beats.title: VII. Storms beyond Tarkir: the collapsing Meditation Realm and Ugin's uncertain future

cards.name: Ugin, Eye of the Storms
cards.why: 2025 modern portrait and emblem of the Spirit Dragon's legacy; NOT evidence he returned bodily to Tarkir from his watch.

cards.name: Call the Spirit Dragons
cards.why: The Stormnexus Ritual and Tarkir's spirit-dragon reawakening, consequences of the world Ugin had altered.

cards.name: Roiling Dragonstorm
cards.why: The continuing storms on Tarkir after Ugin leaves, a key part of the 2025 conflict.

cards.name: Dracogenesis
cards.why: Its Tarkir: Dragonstorm printing directly relates Ugin's survival/death to the magical storms across eras.

cards.name: Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant
cards.why: Sarkhan's 2025 transformation becomes a threat even as Ugin tries and fails to retain Bolas in the vanishing Meditation Realm.

cards.name: Narset's Rebuke
cards.why: Narset's resistance to Sarkhan's Dragonstorm schemes; the contemporary cost of the broken magical balance.

cards.name: The Theorist, Jace Beleren
cards.why: In 2026, Jace's fractured mind develops reality-making techniques in the Meditation Realm, a method he explicitly attributes to Ugin. This is Ugin's intellectual legacy, not proof he is alive or personally present.

cards.name: Death Begets Life
cards.why: Its 2025 Ugin-attributed philosophy is a fitting uncertain epilogue; no source confirms he definitively died or survived in the collapse.

basic_printing_plan: For each basic use one original Dominaria (DOM) and one 2025 Tarkir: Dragonstorm (TDM) illustration if available; these are artistic markers and not extra deck slots.
canon_caveats: The Ur-Dragon is a primordial progenitor, not canonically identified as Ugin's female biological mother.

Ugin's birth occurred on Dominaria; some older Fate Reforged prose calls Tarkir his native plane, which conflicts with later Chronicle of Bolas. This deck follows the more explicit 2018 birth narrative.
Crux of Fate/Bitter Revelation and the five Khans fetch-land flavor texts depict the original Tarkir timeline that Sarkhan rewrote; they must not be mistaken for the surviving continuity.
Ugin and Sorin/Nahiri imprisoned rather than killed the titans; later Gatewatch members killed Ulamog and Kozilek against Ugin's preferred stasis approach.
Azor and the Immortal Sun appear as an ancient flashback whose plan pays off only during the War of the Spark, not as a new 2019 invention.
In the 2019 finale, Bolas was desparked and Ugin served as his jailer in the Meditation Realm.

In the 2025 Tarkir: Dragonstorm story, the Meditation Realm collapsed, Bolas's bonds broke, Ugin tried to hold him, and BOTH disappeared; their survival is explicitly uncertain in the cited story. Do not assert definitive death, rescue, or continuing imprisonment.
The 2026 Reality Fracture story invokes the power of the Meditation Realm in Jace's Echoverse project; this is not evidence Ugin is alive or physically participates.
Emrakul, the Aeons Torn is banned in sanctioned Commander and is retained as a deliberate story-first Rule 0 exception.

The original Ugin, the Spirit Dragon is colorless; the biography's colored allies/antagonists are included because the Ur-Dragon frames WUBRG, not because Ugin was personally color-identified with those cards.
Generic landscape and evocative cards are labeled as locations, consequences, or symbolic portraits rather than fabricated literal appearances.
